newsitem.title: FRANCE: French proud of Chirac, split on Mideast tour.
newsitem.headline: French proud of Chirac, split on Mideast tour.

text.p: French voters are proud that President Jacques Chirac confronted Israeli police in Jerusalem but are split on whether his Middle East tour was a success, according to an opinion poll released on Sunday.

The survey said 83 percent of 937 voters questioned believed Chirac was right to be firm with overzealous Israeli police in a widely-publicised incident during his tour of the Arab Old City of Jerusalem.
French media have called him "battling Chirac" for angrily elbowing his way through the police cordon, comparing him with the valiant Lucky Luke cowboy character of a popular cartoon.
Yet the poll to be published on Monday in the leftwing daily Liberation said 52 percent to 45 percent of voters thought such a public display of anger was not fit for a head of state.

Voters appeared perplexed when asked to pass judgement on the week-long tour of Syria, Israel, Palestinian territories, Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt that Foreign Minister Herve de Charette has called a breakthrough of historical magnitude.
Forty-five percent thought the trip, to seek a place for Europe alongside the United States as co-sponsor of the peace process, was a failure. But 44 percent hailed it as a success.
Fifty-four percent said it had helped the peace process while 43 percent believed the contrary, and 61 percent believed Chirac should have prepared his tour more carefully.
A majority of 53 percent saw France's Middle East policy as well balanced, to 34 percent who said it was pro-Arab and five percent who saw it as pro-Israeli.
An overwhelming majority of 80 percent said France should act in the Middle East as part of joint European Union foreign policy, with 17 percent believing it should go it alone.

Chirac can take comfort from the 57 percent who believed his tour boosted France's image, and from the 41 percent who said it helped his personal standing. Some 24 percent thought it hurt his standing.
